questions.question: A car covers a certain distance at a speed of 45 km/h and returns to the starting point following the same path at a speed of 36 km/h. Find the average speed for the entire journey (in km/h).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed at the time of going = 45 km/h

Speed at the time of return to the starting point = 36 km/h.

**Concept used:**

When distance is constant then,

Average speed = (2xy)/(x + y)

Here,

x = Speed at time of going

y = speed at the time of returning

**Calculation:**

Average speed = (2 × 45 × 36)/(45 + 36) km/hr.

⇒ (2 × 45 × 36)/81 km/hr.

⇒ (3240)/81 km/hr.

⇒ 40 km/hr.

**∴ The average speed for the entire journey (in km/h) is 40.**

questions.question: The ratio of the length, width and height of a cuboid is 60 ∶ 24 ∶ 7 and the length of each of its four space diagonals is 130 cm. What is the volume (*in cm*³) of the cuboid?
questions.solution:

Length : width : height = 60 : 24 : 7

Diagonal = 130 cm

**Concept used:**

d² = l² + b² + h²

Volume of a cuboid = l × b × h

Here,

d = diagonals

l = length

b = breadth or width

h = height

**Calculation:**

Let the length, width, and height of the cuboid be 60x, 24x, 7x

According to the question,

130² = (60x)² + (24x)² + (7x)²

⇒ 16900 = 3600x² + 576x² + 49x²

⇒ 16900 = 4225x2

⇒ x2 = 16900/4225

⇒ x2 = 4

⇒ x = 2

So, length = 60 × 2 = 120 cm

width = 24 × 2 = 48 cm

height = 7 × 2 = 14 cm

Now,

Volume = 120 × 48 × 14

⇒ 80640

So, volume of the cuboid 80640 cm³

**∴ The volume (in cm³) of the cuboid is 80640.**

questions.question: A pipe can fill an empty tank in 12.5 hours. At the bottom of the tank there was a leakage point which can drain the completely filled tank in 17.5 hours. **Given:**

Pipe can fill the tank in 12.5 hours

Leakage can drain in 17.5 hours

**Concept used:**

Total work = Efficiency of the pipe × time taken

**Calculation:**

LCM of 12.5 and 17.5 = 87.5 units i.e total work

So, efficiency of filling pipe = 87.5/12.5

⇒ 7 units/hour

Efficiency of the leakage = 87.5/17.5

⇒ 5 units/hour

Effective efficiency = 7 - 5 [leakage will drain the water so its efficiency will be subtracted from the efficiency of filling the pipe]

⇒ 2 units/hour

So, in 14 hours the tank will be filled by 2 × 14

⇒ 28 units

Remaining = 87.5 - 28

⇒ 59.5 units

Time taken to fill the remaining portion by the filling pipe = 59.5/7

⇒ 8.5 hours

So, total time taken to fill the tank completely = 14 + 8.5

⇒ 22.5 hours.

**∴ The total time taken (in hours) to fill the tank is 22.5.**

Ratio of sides (in plates) = 3 : 4 ⇒ Total plates = 3x × 4x = 12x²

⇒ Actual Length (L) = 8 × 2 cm = 16 cm.

⇒ Third expression = 2 × 2 × 3 × x × x × y × y × z × z × z

⇒ Comparing the numerical coefficients (3, 5, and 12), there are no common prime factors. Thus, their HCF is 1.

⇒ Comparing the variable parts, the common variables that appear in all three expressions are x, y, and z.

⇒ Taking only the common variables corresponding to the lowest exponent available across all expressions gives us 1 × x × y × z.

⇒ Multiplying these gives the overall HCF as xyz.

**∴ The correct answer is xyz.**

Highest Common Factor (HCF) of Polynomials

The HCF is the largest term that divides all the given terms completely. For variable parts, it corresponds to the lowest power (exponent) of each common variable present in all terms.

Least Common Multiple (LCM) of Polynomials

The LCM is the smallest term that is completely divisible by all the given terms. It is obtained by finding the LCM of the numerical coefficients and multiplying it by all variables raised to their highest available powers.

HCF and LCM Relation

For any two mathematical expressions A and B, the product of the two expressions is equal to the product of their HCF and LCM: A × B = HCF(A, B) × LCM(A, B).

questions.question: From the top of a tree 7 m high, the angle of elevation of a tower is 30°. If the tower is 47 m high, how far away from the tower is the tree positioned?

The **height difference** between the **tower** and the **tree** is 47 − 7 = 40 m.

For divisibility by 12, the number must be divisible by both 3 and 4.

questions.question: Two cubes, each having the length of each side as 8 cm, are joined to form a cuboid. What will be the total surface area of the cuboid?

When two cubes are joined, **two faces** (one from each cube) disappear at the junction.

Total faces of two separate cubes = 6 + 6 = 12 faces.

Visible faces of the new **cuboid** = 12 − 2 = 10 faces.

Area of one face = side² = 8² = 64 cm².

Total Surface Area = 10 × 64 = 640 cm².

**∴ The correct answer is 640 cm².**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/93bf782db71143040c57cf43b19ea772f220e93b7fdf694fe09985968653c386.png] 

⇒ **Length (L)** = 8 + 8 = 16 cm

⇒ **Breadth (B)** = 8 cm

⇒ **Height (H)** = 8 cm

⇒ **Total Surface Area (TSA)** of cuboid = 2 × (LB + BH + HL)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (16 × 8 + 8 × 8 + 8 × 16)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (128 + 64 + 128)

⇒ TSA = 2 × (320)

⇒ TSA = 640 cm²

**∴ The correct answer is 640 cm².**

Volume of a Cuboid

The space occupied by the cuboid is calculated as Length × Breadth × Height (V = L × B × H).

Lateral Surface Area (LSA)

The area of the four side walls of a cuboid is given by 2 × H × (L + B).

Diagonal of a Cuboid

The longest rod that can be placed inside a cuboid is √(L² + B² + H²).

Surface Area of a Cube

For a cube with side 'a', the Total Surface Area is 6a² and the Lateral Surface Area is 4a².</p
